verification_note: Both hosts pass the gate. Windows 11 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc: fmt, clippy pedantic with -D warnings in both feature configurations, the whole test suite in both configurations (1358 tests with the default features measured with --all-targets, and 1424 with every feature enabled including the real-window application suite, the GPU islands and the tray), rustdoc with -D warnings, the tools workspace, the client package, and every policy gate. Linux x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu (WSL2, Ubuntu 26.04 LTS): the same gate in its default configuration plus a stage that compiles the release configuration, 23 of 23 stages passing, 52 tests in the tools workspace and the whole workspace suite, run through tools/linux_gate.py with a C compiler assembled from unpacked packages under $HOME because that distro has no toolchain and no root to install one. That gate builds into host-specific target directories for both the workspace and the tools, so a Linux run and a Windows run cannot shadow each other's binaries. It has found a real cross-platform defect every time it has been run: the most recent were an installer written on Unix that had no executable bit, so the file could be built and never run, and `ncui.window.theme`, which was dispatched and offered to pages but left out of the protocol specification's method table, so a client written from the specification would never have learned it existed. The Linux run compiles and *runs* the release configuration: the GTK and WebKit development libraries are installed (an earlier revision of this note wrongly said they were not) and WSLg supplies an X server and a Wayland socket, so the host opens genuine windows — 8 host tests, the 8 page-bridge tests and both comparison ports pass there. That only became true after a real fix: `ncui-webview-wry` created its event loop on a worker thread and set `with_any_thread(true)` on Windows only, so tao's Unix backend panicked on Linux and `ncui run` could not open a window at all. The islands test still needs a GPU device, which the session lacks, so a feature whose evidence needs one stays 'unverified' on Linux. macOS is recorded as 'unverified' and cross_platform.verification.macos as 'not_implemented': no macOS host is reachable, so marking either would be a claim with nothing behind it. Every 'complete' entry was re-checked against the file it cites; the citations that did not survive that check were corrected rather than left standing.

benchmarks.evidence: crates/ncui-state/src/virtualize.rs — the work bound is checked from two directions. a_window_ignores_the_size_of_the_collection_it_is_a_window_into bounds the inspected indices; a_walk_of_every_record_is_caught_even_if_the_counter_is_not_touched bounds wall-clock time at a deep offset, because a self-reported counter is gameable by code that simply does not increment it. Measured by running mutations against the suite: an O(n) index_at and an overscan scaled by the collection size are both caught.
